record.final_answer:
No. I couldn't find any published numbers for Marrowlog over TLS.

**What exists:** the maintainers' own Marrowlog 2.4 report for 2026 Q2 (https://marrowlog.example/perf/2026-q2, published 2026-06-18). It says one agent shipped **180,000 lines/s on 1 vCPU, with CPU at 85%**. That figure is the median of three 30-minute runs. It doesn't fit your case:

- **TLS was off in every run.** The report lists TLS as not measured and says it's planned for the Q4 report.
- **Every line was 200 bytes or shorter.** The README says your lines average about 900 bytes, and the report also lists longer lines as not measured.
- Disk buffer off and `batch_lines: 500`. These match `config/agent.yaml`, so they're the one part that does fit.

**Checked today:** the Q2 page hasn't changed. I guessed the URLs `/perf/2026-q3` and `/perf/2026-q4` and both return 404, so I found no Q4 report. One may exist somewhere else on their site.

**My own estimate, not from the report:** by bytes, your peak is 50,000 × 900 B ≈ 45 MB/s. The report's run was at most 180,000 × 200 B ≈ 36 MB/s. So even on plain TCP your load is beyond what they tested, and TLS adds encryption work on the same single vCPU. The 180k figure looks like a lot of headroom, but it doesn't show the agent can handle 50k lines/s over TLS.

**Suggestion:** run your own test on a 1-vCPU agent with `tls: true`, replaying your real ~900-byte JSON lines at 50k/s. Watch CPU use and whether the agent falls behind the log files. You could also ask the maintainers when the Q4 TLS report is coming out.

I added today's check to the existing memory note on this report, so a later session won't redo it.
